title: ci: build the extra package formats in follow-up pipelines after a release, then add them to the release page

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
The maintainer asked for this work, in his own words (2026-11-18):

> we should build things like AUR packages, RPM, DEB and the "non-standard" style of packages- after a release.. once release triggers, that should trigger secondary pipelines focused on all the weird package formats, and then backfill the releases backpage after the fact..

## Problem

`release.yml` builds the core artifacts (zip, installer, wasm site) and some package formats (`aur`, `snap`, `flatpak`) in the same run. A slow or broken package job holds the release run open. A failed package job makes the run red, but the release itself is fine. The v0.24.0 run showed this: the `aur` job was still running after all other jobs were green.

## Wanted

1. `release.yml` publishes the core release first. The core is the zip, the installer and the site. It does not wait for the extra formats.
2. The release start triggers secondary workflows. Each workflow builds one family of formats: AUR, RPM, DEB, snap, flatpak and other non-standard formats.
3. Each secondary workflow attaches its artifact to the existing GitHub release after the fact (backfill). It does not move or re-push the tag.
4. A failed secondary workflow does not change the state of the release. It reports its own failure and can run again for one tag (`workflow_dispatch` with a tag input).
5. The release notes or the download page list each format that is attached. A format that is not attached yet is not listed as available.

## Constraints

- AGENTS.md "GitHub Actions minutes are budgeted": a new `push`, `pull_request` or `schedule` trigger needs the maintainer's approval. Use `workflow_run` or `workflow_dispatch` started by the release run. Name the trigger in the PR body.
- A secondary workflow on a self-hosted runner must never start from a fork PR (`runners` skill).
- Keep the existing `aur-package.yml` and the `aur`, `snap` and `flatpak` jobs working until their replacement is proven on a real tag. Never test on a published tag. Use a throwaway tag in a fork or `dry_run`.
- Do not change the cut procedure: the cut is complete when the tag is on GitHub and `release.yml` attached the core artifact. Update the `release-cut` and `runners` skills for the new flow (a process change: `Process change: yes`).
- Related: #2590 (ship `camcraft-sim` in the packages).

## Done means

- A release tag starts the core run and the secondary workflows.
- The core release is complete before the first secondary workflow ends.
- Each secondary workflow adds its artifact to the same release and can run again for one tag.
- The `release-cut` and `runners` skills describe the flow.
- A decision file in `docs/decisions/` records which formats are in the first slice and which are later.
